newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mandela says in prison he moved to keep talks secret.
newsitem.headline: Mandela says in prison he moved to keep talks secret.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela said on Tuesday that alert prison warders suspicious of his unexplained meetings with top government officials forced his move to another prison to keep the meetings secret in the run-up to the end of apartheid.

"Warders would often ask me after hours of negotiations with government where I had been," Mandela told reporters on a visit to the Victor Verster prison house where he spent the last two years of his 27-year incarceration.
"Because it was clear people were beginning to suspect what was going on and because it was difficult to keep the negotiations secret, it was decided I should be moved to here," he added.

The secret meetings, which started in 1985 at Cape Town's Pollsmoor Prison after his transfer from notorious Robben Island prison, eventually paved the way for South Africa's first all-race elections in 1994.

In his autobiography Mandela says the meetings were kept secret because it was thought the political climate at the time was not right to announce them. Mandela at the time was the head of the banned African National Congress, which has led the government since the 1994 elections.
Mandela was moved to the house, situated in the grounds of a prison farm near the picturesque rural town of Paarl, in 1988. It had previously been occupied by a prison warder.
He shared it three prison warders and could receive visitors. The warders sometimes took him on drives throughout the Western Cape, he said.
Asked by a reporter if he was never inclined to escape during one of those outing, he said the responsibility of seeing the negotiations through had been too great.
